intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental
experiences.description: Explore the grand 14th-century Joseon dynasty palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok. Renting a Hanbok grants free entry to the palace and makes for stunning photos at one of Seoul's most iconic landmarks. Witness the ceremonial changing of the royal guard and wander through the National Folk Museum on the palace grounds.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Seoul's legendary food scene at one of Korea's oldest and largest traditional markets. Sample iconic local dishes including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare) straight from the market stalls. A true feast for the senses and a must for any food lover.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Experience & SMTOWN Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the heart of K-culture at SMTOWN COEX Artium, an interactive K-pop museum and entertainment complex. Enjoy hologram concerts, explore exhibits dedicated to top K-pop groups like EXO, aespa, and NCT, browse exclusive merchandise, and even try a K-pop dance lesson at a nearby studio in the same district. Perfect for any K-culture enthusiast.

experiences.name: Insadong & Bukchon Hanok Village Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through the charming, lantern-lined streets of Insadong, Seoul's cultural arts district, browsing traditional tea houses, indie craft shops, and galleries. Then walk uphill to Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved neighborhood of 600-year-old traditional Korean houses (hanok) with sweeping views over the city. Stop for a bowl of traditional bingsu (shaved ice dessert) along the way.

experiences.name: Hongdae Night Out & Street Culture Experience
experiences.description: Experience the electric energy of Hongdae, Seoul's youth culture and indie arts hub. Watch spontaneous K-pop busking performances, explore vibrant street art murals, shop at quirky vintage and K-fashion boutiques, and enjoy live music at intimate indie venues. Cap the night with Korean fried chicken and craft beer at a local pojangmacha (street tent bar) — the quintessential Seoul night experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — skip morning slot. Take AREX (Airport Railroad Express) to Seoul Station (~43 min, ~₩9,500). Transfer via subway Line 3 to Gyeongbokgung Station. Check into boutique stay, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Short walk to explore the immediate Gyeongbokgung neighborhood. Stroll along Gyeongbokgung Palace's outer walls and Sejong-daero boulevard. Stop at Gwanghwamun Square to see the Yi Sun-sin and King Sejong statues — free and iconic first impressions of Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Tongin Market (10-min walk) for a budget-friendly dinner browsing street food stalls. Try tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), hotteok (sweet pancakes), and bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes). Pick up a T-money card at a convenience store (GS25 or CU) for subway travel throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a light snack at Incheon Airport convenience store (~₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Grab kimbap or a triangle rice ball at a GS25/CU convenience store near Seoul Station (~₩2,000–4,000)
meals.dinner: Tongin Market street food — budget ₩6,000–10,000 for a satisfying mix of snacks and small bites

day_by_day.notes: Priority on Day 1: charge T-money card (minimum ₩10,000), screenshot hotel address in Korean for taxi backup, and rest early to beat jet lag. December in Seoul is cold (0–5°C), so wear thermal layers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (₩3,000 entry) when it opens at 9:00 AM. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM at Gwanghwamun Gate — free and spectacular in winter. Rent a hanbok at one of the nearby shops (~₩15,000–20,000/hr) for free palace entry and great photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north through the palace to explore Bukchon Hanok Village — a maze of traditional Korean hanok houses. Wander the alleyways, peek into craft shops, and enjoy the stunning contrast of old rooftops against modern Seoul. Visit Gahoe-dong's famous photo spot on the hillside lane.
day_by_day.evening: Walk south to Insadong for dinner and evening browsing. Explore Ssamziegil courtyard complex for indie shops and K-culture souvenirs. Try street food from vendors along Insadong-gil.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near hotel — triangle kimbap + instant coffee (~₩3,500)
meals.lunch: Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) at a local restaurant near Bukchon (~₩12,000–15,000) — warming and iconic in winter
meals.dinner: Insadong street food: hotteok, dakkochi (chicken skewers), and tteokbokki (~₩6,000–8,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays — Day 2 falls on Wednesday so it's open. Hanbok rental shops open around 9:00 AM. Bukchon is a residential area — keep noise low out of respect for residents.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 3 to Anguk Station and visit Changdeokgung Palace (₩3,000) including the Secret Garden (Huwon) if available in winter — check seasonal schedule. The garden is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and hauntingly beautiful in December frost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Changgyeonggung Palace (₩1,000) next door for a quieter, less-crowded experience. Then head to Jongmyo Shrine (₩1,000) — the solemn royal ancestral shrine and another UNESCO site. The minimalist architecture is deeply moving.
day_by_day.evening: Take the subway to Dongdaemun (Line 1 or 4). Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — the futuristic Zaha Hadid-designed building is free to walk around and beautifully lit at night. Browse Dongdaemun Market for budget fashion and accessories.

meals.breakfast: Congee (juk) at a local juk restaurant near Anguk Station (~₩7,000–9,000) — perfect warm winter breakfast
meals.lunch: Bibimbap at a small local restaurant near Changdeokgung (~₩8,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun Market food stalls: sundae (Korean blood sausage), eomuk (fish cake soup), ramyeon (~₩5,000–8,000)

day_by_day.notes: Jongmyo Shrine guided tours run at set times — check the schedule at the entrance. DDP is open late and the light installations in December are especially festive. Wear very warm shoes as you'll be walking on cold stone all day.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 4 to Myeongdong. Explore Myeongdong Cathedral (free entry, beautiful Gothic architecture) in the morning before crowds arrive. Browse Myeongdong's famous street food alley — vendors set up by 10:00 AM with egg bread, tornado potatoes, and lobster skewers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk uphill to Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower). Take the cable car (~₩9,500 round trip) or hike up the Namsan trail (free, ~30 min). Enjoy panoramic winter views of Seoul. See the famous love padlocks fence. Tower observatory entry ~₩21,000 — optional, views from the deck below are free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Myeongdong for the evening street food market — the best time as vendors are fully set up. Browse K-beauty shops (Innisfree, Etude, Olive Young) for affordable skincare souvenirs. Take subway back to Gyeongbokgung area.

meals.breakfast: Myeongdong street food breakfast: egg bread (gyeran-ppang) + hotteok (~₩4,000)
meals.lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja restaurant — famous kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) for ~₩10,000, expect a queue but worth it
meals.dinner: Myeongdong evening street stalls: lobster skewer, tteokbokki, odeng soup (~₩8,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings in Myeongdong are very crowded — embrace the energy. Olive Young is the best place for affordable K-beauty products. Skip the N Seoul Tower observatory if budget is tight — the free outdoor deck has great views.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 2 to Hongdae (Hongik University Station). Explore the vibrant Hongdae street art district — murals, indie boutiques, and quirky cafés. Visit the Trick Eye Museum (~₩15,000) for interactive 3D art experiences popular in K-culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Yeonnam-dong neighborhood — a hipster enclave with independent cafés, vintage shops, and trendy restaurants. Perfect for experiencing contemporary Seoul youth culture. Visit Gyeongui Line Forest Park (Yeonnam-dong section) — a converted railway line turned green walkway.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the Saturday evening street performance scene near the main plaza. Local buskers, dance crews, and musicians perform from around 6:00 PM. Have dinner in the area and enjoy the lively K-culture nightlife atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Hongdae — a popular local bakery like Paris Baguette or a small indie café (~₩5,000–7,000)
meals.lunch: Yeonnam-dong local restaurant — try kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew) set meal (~₩8,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae pojangmacha (street tent bar) — dakbal (spicy chicken feet) or samgyeopsal (pork belly) with soju (~₩12,000–15,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the best day to experience Hongdae's street performance culture. The area is extremely popular with both locals and tourists. Budget extra for the Trick Eye Museum if interested in K-culture experiences — it's very Instagram-worthy.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 2 to Sinchon or Ewha Womans University Station. Explore the Ewha campus (free, open to public) — beautiful Gothic architecture and a famous underground shopping street. Browse the surrounding Sinchon area's vintage clothing shops and indie record stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seodaemun Prison History Hall (₩3,000) — a sobering but essential cultural site documenting Korea's independence movement during Japanese colonial rule. Deeply important for understanding Korean identity and modern history.
day_by_day.evening: Take the subway to Gyeongbokgung area and explore the Tongin Market area at dusk. Try the famous Tongin Market Dosirak Café experience — buy old-style brass coins (~₩5,000 for 10 coins) and use them to purchase small dishes from vendors to fill your own lunchbox (available until closing ~7:00 PM).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area convenience store or nearby bakery (~₩4,000–6,000)
meals.lunch: Sinchon area local restaurant — doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew) set (~₩8,000)
meals.dinner: Tongin Market dosirak experience (~₩5,000–8,000 for a full tray of various banchan and dishes)

day_by_day.notes: Seodaemun Prison is closed on Mondays — visiting on Sunday is ideal. The Tongin Market dosirak coin café closes early (around 5–7 PM) so plan accordingly. Sunday markets can be lively — great day for people-watching.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 2 to Gangnam Station. Walk along Garosu-gil (Tree-lined Road) — a fashionable boulevard with independent boutiques, galleries, and cafés. Window-shop and absorb the upscale but walkable Gangnam culture without spending much.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit COEX Mall (free to enter) — a massive underground shopping complex. Find the famous COEX Starfield Library (free) — a stunning floor-to-ceiling bookshelf installation that's a beloved Seoul landmark. Browse the K-pop merchandise stores inside.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to nearby SM Town COEX Artium (free to browse ground floor) — the SM Entertainment flagship store with K-pop merchandise, a museum floor, and a café. Great for K-culture fans. Take subway back via Line 2.

meals.breakfast: Gangnam area convenience store or café (~₩4,000–6,000)
meals.lunch: COEX food court — wide variety of Korean dishes at reasonable prices (~₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Gangnam local gukbap (rice soup) restaurant — soondae gukbap or dwaeji gukbap (~₩8,000–9,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gangnam is pricier than other neighborhoods — stick to the food court and free sights to keep budget in check. The Starfield Library is one of Seoul's most photogenic spots. SM Town store is best for K-pop fans — BTS fans should note HYBE is in a different location.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 3 to Gyeongbokgung area and visit the National Folk Museum of Korea (free with palace ticket or ₩3,000 separately) — excellent exhibits on traditional Korean daily life, customs, and festivals. Very relevant for understanding K-culture roots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Museum of Korea (free entry) — take subway Line 4 to Ichon Station. One of Asia's largest museums with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts, Buddhist art, and royal treasures. Budget 2–3 hours minimum.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Itaewon area (subway Line 6, Itaewon Station) for a multicultural evening. Browse the Gyeongnidan-gil (Gyongni-dan-gil) side street — a trendy strip of international restaurants and indie bars. Great for experiencing Seoul's cosmopolitan side.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area local bakery or café (~₩5,000)
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria — affordable Korean set meals (~₩8,000–10,000) with a view of the garden
meals.dinner: Gyeongnidan-gil area — try a local Korean-fusion restaurant or affordable international option (~₩10,000–14,000)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is free and world-class — don't skip it. Tuesday is when Gyeongbokgung Palace is closed, so this is the perfect day to visit the museums instead. Itaewon has become more locally-oriented in recent years — Gyeongnidan-gil is the best part to explore.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 1 to Jongno 3-ga, then walk to Nakwon Arcade — the legendary multi-story musical instrument market. Browse traditional Korean instruments (haegeum, gayageum, janggu drums) alongside modern guitars. Then visit Tapgol Park (free) — a historically significant park with the original Declaration of Independence site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a beautifully preserved hanok alley turned into trendy cafés and boutiques. More intimate and less touristy than Bukchon. Great for K-drama atmosphere and unique café experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Jongno area for Christmas Eve Eve atmosphere — Seoul decorates heavily for Christmas. Visit the Cheonggyecheon Stream (free) — a restored urban stream with beautiful winter light installations running through downtown Seoul. Walk the 5.8km stream path under the city lights.

meals.breakfast: Jongno area local restaurant — haejang-guk (hangover soup/hearty beef bone broth, ~₩8,000) — a classic Korean morning meal
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong café lunch — a trendy café offering light Korean fusion meals (~₩10,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Cheonggyecheon area pojangmacha or nearby bunsik (casual Korean snack restaurant) — ramyeon, kimbap, mandu (~₩6,000–8,000)

day_by_day.notes: Ikseon-dong is extremely photogenic and popular — visit on a weekday morning to avoid weekend crowds. The Cheonggyecheon Stream light festival (Lantern Festival) sometimes runs into December — check the schedule as it may still be active and is completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Take subway Line 2 to Sindorim, transfer to Line 1 to Yeongdeungpo, then explore Times Square Mall (free to enter) — a massive shopping complex with a famous Christmas tree display. Alternatively, visit Yeouido Hangang Park (subway Line 5, Yeouido Station) for winter riverside views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Han River (Hangang) at Yeouido for a winter afternoon stroll. Rent a bicycle (~₩3,000/hr) from the Hangang Park rental station if weather permits, or simply walk along the frozen-adjacent riverside. The winter Han River scenery is quintessentially Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul — experience the festive atmosphere in Myeongdong or near City Hall Plaza where large Christmas trees and light displays are set up. Koreans celebrate Christmas Eve as a romantic holiday — the city is beautifully lit. Attend a Christmas Eve service at Myeongdong Cathedral (free, check schedule).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area convenience store festive snacks (~₩4,000–6,000)
meals.lunch: Yeouido area local restaurant — galbitang (beef short rib soup, ~₩10,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Christmas Eve street food + a sit-down restaurant treat — budget ₩15,000–20,000 for a slightly special Christmas Eve meal (Korean BBQ at a budget joint)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of Seoul's most festive nights — expect crowds in Myeongdong and City Hall. It's a romantic holiday in Korea (like Valentine's Day) so the atmosphere is very lively. Book a restaurant in advance if you want a sit-down dinner as popular spots fill up.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (free, 10-min walk from hotel area) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in Seoul. Beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round. A peaceful and culturally rich contrast to the Christmas festivities outside. Observe morning prayer rituals respectfully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take subway Line 3 to Gyeongbokgung and visit the National Palace Museum of Korea (free) — adjacent to the palace, it houses royal artifacts, ceramics, and court culture exhibits. Quiet on Christmas Day as many tourists are elsewhere.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming neighborhood of independent cafés, art galleries, and traditional houses. Many artists and writers have lived here. Browse the small galleries and warm up in a traditional tea house (dahyang) with a bowl of yujacha (citron tea, ~₩5,000).

meals.breakfast: Seochon or hotel area café — patbingsu (red bean porridge, called patjuk in winter) is a traditional Christmas food in Korea (~₩5,000–7,000)
meals.lunch: National Palace Museum area — nearby local restaurant for doenjang jjigae set (~₩9,000)
meals.dinner: Seochon Village cozy restaurant — try budae jjigae (army stew, a Korean-American fusion dish, ~₩10,000–13,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day (December 25) is a national holiday in South Korea — most major sights are open but some smaller shops may be closed. Jogyesa Temple is always open and free. Patjuk (red bean porridge) is traditionally eaten on the winter solstice (December 22) but widely available through Christmas week.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway (Line 1) to Suwon Station, then local bus or taxi to Hwaseong Fortress (₩1,000 entry) — a stunning UNESCO World Heritage walled fortress from the Joseon Dynasty. Walk the full 5.7km fortress wall circuit for panoramic views. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Haenggung Palace (₩1,500) inside the fortress walls — a secondary royal palace with well-preserved halls. Suwon is also famous for galbi (grilled short ribs) — a perfect lunch stop. Return to Seoul via subway in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Seoul, visit Gwangjang Market (subway Line 1 or 2, Jongno 5-ga Station) — one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. The evening food market is legendary: bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive small kimbap rolls), and raw beef yukhoe (beef tartare).

meals.breakfast: Quick convenience store meal before early departure (~₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (grilled short ribs) near Hwaseong Fortress — a regional specialty (~₩15,000–20,000, slight splurge but iconic)
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market — bindaetteok, mayak kimbap, eomuk, and soju (~₩10,000–15,000 for a full spread)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon is about 1 hour from Seoul by subway — leave by 8:30 AM to maximize time. The full Hwaseong fortress wall walk takes about 2 hours at a leisurely pace. Gwangjang Market is one of the most authentic food market experiences in Korea — go hungry.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning walk around Gyeongbokgung neighborhood. Visit any missed spots near the hotel — Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House, former presidential residence, now open to public, free) is a 15-minute walk from the hotel and offers a final dose of Korean history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of hotel. Take subway Line 3 to Seoul Station, then AREX to Incheon Airport (~43 min). Arrive at airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Use remaining won at airport convenience stores or duty-free shops.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast near hotel — a local haejang-guk or sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) restaurant (~₩8,000–10,000)
meals.lunch: Airport food court at Incheon — try one last bowl of Korean ramen or bibimbap (~₩10,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: On the flight

day_by_day.notes: Return any unused T-money card balance at the airport — you can get a refund minus a small fee at T-money refund kiosks in Incheon Airport. Pack any food souvenirs (instant tteokbokki, Korean ramen, seaweed snacks) in checked luggage. Budget tip: total estimated daily spend excluding accommodation is approximately ₩30,000–50,000 (€20–35) per day for food and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — clear customs, collect luggage, and take the AREX Express Train to Seoul Station (approx. 43 min, ~₩9,500). Transfer to hotel in Gyeongbokgung area via subway or taxi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the Boutique Stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu. Freshen up, then take a gentle orientation stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village (10–15 min walk from hotel) — admire the traditional Korean hanok rooftops and narrow alleyways at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong Street for your first taste of Seoul's cultural atmosphere — browse art galleries, craft shops, and street stalls. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick snack at Incheon Airport (Paris Baguette or convenience store onigiri)
meals.lunch: Light meal at Seoul Station food court or a convenience store bento box while settling in
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌 삼계탕) near Gyeongbokgung — warming ginseng chicken soup, perfect after a long flight (~₩17,000)

day_by_day.notes: December in Seoul is cold (0°C to -5°C). Pack thermal layers, a heavy coat, gloves, and a scarf. Day 1 is intentionally light — rest and acclimatize. Keep transit cards (T-money) topped up.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace first thing (opens 09:00, ~₩3,000 entry) — explore the grand throne hall Geunjeongjeon, the scenic Hyangwonjeong Pavilion, and catch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 and 14:00. Dress in hanbok for free entry and great photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the National Folk Museum of Korea inside the palace grounds (free with palace ticket). Then head to Gyeonghuigung Palace or stroll up to Cheongwadae (Blue House) area for a scenic walk along the newly opened presidential grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwanghwamun Square area for the winter light festival displays. Explore the underground Gwanghwamun shopping arcade to warm up.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — try a Korean-style breakfast set with doenjang jjigae (soybean paste soup) at a local sikdang
meals.lunch: Gwanghwamun Gukbap (광화문국밥) near the palace — hearty pork rice soup, a Seoul institution (~₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Samgyeopsal BBQ at a local grill restaurant in Jongno-gu — pork belly with banchan sides (~₩15,000–20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays — since today is Wednesday, it's open. Arrive early to beat crowds and get the best photos of the palace in morning light against the Bugaksan mountain backdrop.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and the Secret Garden (Huwon) — book the Secret Garden tour in advance online (~₩8,000). The winter-bare trees and frozen ponds create a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere. The guided tour lasts about 90 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Changgyeonggung Palace and Jongmyo Shrine (UNESCO World Heritage Site, ~₩1,000) — the ancestral shrine of the Joseon dynasty kings, serene and deeply historical.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a trendy neighborhood of converted hanok houses turned into indie cafés, cocktail bars, and boutique shops. Perfect for a cool evening wander.

meals.breakfast: Café Bora or a nearby bakery in Insadong for matcha latte and pastries
meals.lunch: Jongno Bindaetteok (종로 빈대떡) at Gwangjang Market — mung bean pancakes and tteokbokki at market stalls (~₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Modern Korean cuisine at a restaurant in Ikseon-dong — try Korean fusion bibimbap or galbi jjim (braised short ribs) (~₩18,000–25,000)

day_by_day.notes: Jongmyo Shrine is only fully open on weekdays and the first Sunday of each month for individual visitors. The Secret Garden tour has limited spots — book at least a day ahead on the official website.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Bukhansan National Park (Gupabal or Dobongsan entrance) for a morning hike. The Dulegil Trail (둘레길 circular trail) offers a manageable winter walk with stunning mountain and city views. Dress in layers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan (free entry, open until 18:00) — one of Asia's largest museums, covering 5,000 years of Korean history with stunning artifacts including the Goryeo celadon collection.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Itaewon / Haebangchon (HBC) area for a vibrant Friday evening — multicultural neighborhood with great bars, international restaurants, and a lively K-culture nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store (GS25 or CU) breakfast — triangle kimbap, hot coffee, and a warm egg sandwich (~₩5,000)
meals.lunch: Post-hike meal at a mountain trail restaurant (sangjip) near Bukhansan — doenjang jjigae set meal (~₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Haebangchon neighborhood restaurant — try Korean fried chicken (chimaek) with a cold Hite or Cass beer at a pojangmacha-style spot (~₩20,000)

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan trails can be icy in December — wear hiking boots with good grip or bring micro-spikes. The National Museum closes on Mondays, so Friday is perfect. Friday evening in Itaewon is lively — great for experiencing Seoul's nightlife culture.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gwangjang Market (광장시장) — one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic traditional markets. Try iconic street foods: mayak gimbap (addictive sesame rice rolls), bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), and sundae (blood sausage). A true foodie experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll along Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) — a beautiful urban stream walkway lined with winter light installations. Walk from the Cheonggye Plaza toward the east for about 2km, then explore the surrounding Euljiro district known for its indie cafés and retro-industrial vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — the iconic Zaha Hadid-designed building is spectacular at night. Check out the winter design market or exhibitions inside, and browse the surrounding Dongdaemun fashion district.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market food stalls — mayak gimbap and a bowl of kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout soup) (~₩8,000)
meals.lunch: Euljiro 3-ga area — try a retro-style Korean set lunch at one of the old-school restaurants hidden in the alleyways (~₩10,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area — Jokbal (pig's trotter) or Haemul Pajeon (seafood pancake) at a local restaurant (~₩15,000–20,000)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day at Gwangjang Market — arrive before 10:00 to avoid the biggest crowds. Cheonggyecheon is especially beautiful in December evenings with the Seoul Lantern Festival lights (if the festival overlaps with your visit dates).

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Namsangol Hanok Village (남산골 한옥마을) — a free open-air folk village near Namsan Mountain with restored traditional houses, cultural performances, and a time capsule plaza. A peaceful Sunday morning activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Namsan Cable Car (~₩12,000 round trip) up to N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) — enjoy panoramic 360° views of Seoul in winter. Browse the famous love locks fence and visit the observation deck (~₩21,000).
day_by_day.evening: Descend to Myeongdong — Seoul's most famous shopping and street food district. Sunday evening is electric here. Browse cosmetics shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), street food carts, and neon-lit boutiques.

meals.breakfast: Nearby hotel area café — try a traditional Korean breakfast of juk (rice porridge) at Bon Juk restaurant (~₩9,000)
meals.lunch: Namsangol Village area — packed lunch or nearby restaurant with kimchi jjigae set (~₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food feast — try hotteok (sweet pancakes), tteokbokki, odeng (fish cake skewers), and Korean corn dogs (~₩15,000 total for a satisfying street food dinner)

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower is romantic and iconic but can be windy and very cold in December — dress warmly. Myeongdong on Sunday evening is extremely busy; keep your belongings secure. Many K-beauty shops offer free samples — a great way to explore Korean skincare culture.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Palace Museum of Korea (국립고궁박물관) — located just outside Gyeongbokgung, free entry, with exquisite royal artifacts from the Joseon dynasty. Spend 2 hours exploring at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — Seoul's youth culture hub. Explore the indie shops, K-pop merchandise stores, record shops, and street art murals. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or LINE Friends flagship store for fun K-culture experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the evening — the area comes alive with buskers, live music, and street performers. Explore the nightlife strip and enjoy a K-indie music performance at a small live venue (club FF or Gopchang Jeongol area).

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or Jongno — try a hearty haejang-guk (hangover soup) at a local spot, great for cold mornings (~₩10,000)
meals.lunch: Hongdae area — Korean army stew (budae jjigae) at a traditional restaurant, a quirky fusion dish with Korean and American influences (~₩14,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae late dinner — gopchang (grilled intestines) or dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) at a casual restaurant (~₩15,000–18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Monday is a good day for museums as most are open (National Palace Museum is closed on Tuesdays). Hongdae is best experienced from late afternoon onwards when the energy picks up. December 21 is the Winter Solstice — the shortest day, so expect darkness by 17:30.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원 화성) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour south of Seoul by subway. Walk the 5.7km fortress wall circuit for stunning views, and visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace inside the fortress grounds (~₩1,500 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's traditional market near the fortress — try the famous Suwon galbi (beef short ribs, a local specialty). Browse the old town streets around Paldalmun Gate.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and spend the evening in the Sinchon / Yonsei University area — a student neighborhood with affordable restaurants, norebang (karaoke) rooms, and a youthful vibe.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel or convenience store before departing for Suwon
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi at a traditional restaurant near Hwaseong — the city's most famous dish, grilled beef ribs (~₩25,000–30,000, worth the splurge)
meals.dinner: Sinchon area — affordable Korean comfort food at a university-area restaurant: kimchi fried rice or ramyeon hot pot (~₩8,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Take subway Line 1 directly to Suwon Station (about 60 min from Seoul Station). From Suwon Station, take a local bus or taxi to the fortress. The fortress walk is exposed and windy in December — dress in your warmest layers. Note: Gyeongbokgung is closed today (Tuesday) so this day trip is perfectly timed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art in Hannam-dong — one of Korea's finest private art museums featuring traditional Korean art alongside contemporary works by artists like Damien Hirst and Jeff Koons (~₩20,000). Architecturally stunning buildings by Rem Koolhaas, Mario Botta, and Jean Nouvel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hannam-dong and Itaewon's upscale boutique district — browse concept stores, independent Korean fashion designers, and international galleries. Walk along the Hannam-daero street for a more refined shopping experience than Myeongdong.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve Eve in Seoul — experience the festive holiday atmosphere in Gangnam's Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Cheongdam-dong. See luxury brand flagship stores decorated for Christmas and enjoy the glamorous side of Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Hannam-dong specialty café — Seoul has world-class specialty coffee culture; try a local roaster like Fritz Coffee or Felt Coffee (~₩7,000)
meals.lunch: Itaewon — Korean-Japanese fusion at a local restaurant or a bowl of authentic ramen (~₩13,000–16,000)
meals.dinner: Cheongdam-dong or Apgujeong — treat yourself to a nicer dinner at a Korean modern cuisine restaurant; try galbi or bulgogi course meal (~₩35,000–50,000 as a mid-range splurge)

day_by_day.notes: December 23 in Seoul will have Christmas decorations and festive lights everywhere — perfect for evening photography. Gangnam is best explored in the afternoon and evening when shops are fully open. Keep receipts for VAT refund at the airport (available for purchases over ₩30,000 at participating stores).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) in Jongno — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round and especially atmospheric in winter. Attend a morning service or simply explore the grounds peacefully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Seochon Village (서촌) neighborhood — a quieter, more authentic alternative to Bukchon, with independent bookshops, art studios, traditional teahouses, and the former homes of Korean artists and poets. Visit Sejong Museum of Art (Sejong Center).
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul — Koreans celebrate Christmas as a romantic holiday. Head to Myeongdong Cathedral (명동성당) for the midnight mass atmosphere and beautiful exterior lights. The streets of Myeongdong are magical on Christmas Eve.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean tea and rice cake (tteok) at a hanok teahouse in Seochon (~₩8,000)
meals.lunch: Seochon neighborhood — try a charming set lunch at a local Korean restaurant in a converted hanok (~₩13,000–16,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — enjoy a festive dinner at a mid-range Korean restaurant in Myeongdong; try a hot pot (jeongol) course for a warming Christmas Eve meal (~₩25,000–30,000)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the busiest nights in Seoul — restaurants fill up quickly, so make a reservation for dinner. Myeongdong Cathedral hosts a Christmas Eve mass (midnight mass) which is open to all visitors regardless of religion — a beautiful cultural experience. Many couples exchange gifts and enjoy the romantic atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning — visit the quiet and beautiful Changgyeonggung Palace gardens for a peaceful winter morning walk. The bare trees and frozen lotus pond are hauntingly beautiful. Entry ~₩1,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Lotte World (롯데월드) in Jamsil — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks. Christmas Day here is festive and magical with special decorations, performances, and seasonal attractions. Day pass ~₩62,000. Alternatively, visit the nearby Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory (123 floors, ~₩29,000) for incredible views.
day_by_day.evening: Jamsil area — explore the Seokchon Lake Park surrounding Lotte World Tower, beautifully lit for Christmas. The lake reflections of the tower lights are spectacular for photos.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a Christmas morning brunch at a café near the hotel — many Seoul cafés do special Christmas menus
meals.lunch: Lotte World food court or a restaurant inside the complex — Korean fried chicken or a hearty stew (~₩15,000–18,000)
meals.dinner: Jamsil area — try a Christmas dinner at a galmaegi-sal (pork skirt meat) BBQ restaurant, a fun and social Korean Christmas dinner style (~₩20,000)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas is a public holiday in South Korea — most attractions and restaurants are open, but some smaller shops may be closed. Lotte World is very popular on Christmas Day — arrive early or book tickets online in advance. The Seokchon Lake light show is free and runs into January.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) in Yongsan — free entry to this powerful and comprehensive museum covering Korean military history, with particular focus on the Korean War. The outdoor exhibition of tanks, aircraft, and artillery is impressive even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gangnam's COEX Mall — Asia's largest underground shopping mall. Browse the famous Starfield Library inside (a stunning public library within the mall), K-pop merchandise stores, aquarium, and high-end shops. Perfect for last-minute souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Seoul — head to Han River (Hangang) Banpo Bridge area for the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain (check if winter schedule is running). Then enjoy a final Korean BBQ dinner to celebrate your trip.

meals.breakfast: Yongsan area — Korean-style breakfast at a local sikdang near the War Memorial (~₩9,000)
meals.lunch: COEX food hall — wide variety of Korean and international options; try a Korean set meal or bibimbap (~₩12,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Farewell Korean BBQ dinner — Chadolbaegi (thinly sliced beef brisket) at a quality BBQ restaurant in Gangnam or back in Jongno (~₩25,000–35,000 per person with side dishes and soju)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is your last full day — use the morning for any remaining sightseeing and the afternoon for final shopping and souvenir purchases. Myeongdong and COEX are great for last-minute K-beauty, K-pop merchandise, Korean snacks (Pepero, Choco Pie, seaweed), and traditional crafts. Keep receipts for VAT refund at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Gyeongbokgung area — take one last walk through Bukchon Hanok Village at sunrise for beautiful, quiet photos without the crowds. Visit a nearby café for a final Korean coffee and patbingsu (if available) or a warm sikhye (sweet rice drink).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (standard checkout 11:00 — arrange late checkout or luggage storage if needed). Head to the airport: take the subway to Seoul Station and board the AREX Express Train to Incheon Airport (43 min, ~₩9,500). Arrive at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in, security, and VAT refund processing.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Korean ginseng, cosmetics, and snacks. Enjoy a final bowl of Korean noodles at the airport food court before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast near the hotel — try a sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) set at a local restaurant (~₩10,000), a perfect warm farewell to Seoul
meals.lunch: Light meal at Seoul Station or Incheon Airport — airport food court has excellent Korean options including bibimbap and ramyeon (~₩12,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining before departure

day_by_day.notes: Submit VAT refund claims at the airport before check-in (for amounts over ₩30,000 from participating stores — look for the Global Blue or Korea Tax Free logo). Incheon Airport is massive — allow extra time to navigate. The AREX train from Seoul Station departs every 30 minutes. Don't forget to return your T-money card for a deposit refund at the airport convenience store. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — skip morning slot. Private luxury transfer arranged via premium chauffeur service from ICN to boutique stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu (approx. 60–75 min). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your hanok-inspired boutique accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll through the Gyeongbokgung neighborhood. Visit the iconic Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds for a late-afternoon walk along the outer walls and the Heungnyemun Gate area. Stop at the National Folk Museum of Korea (open until 18:00) for a soft introduction to Korean history and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric Bukchon Hanok Village lantern-lit alleys at dusk for a magical first impression of traditional Seoul. Enjoy a welcome dinner at Jungsik (two Michelin stars, Gangnam) — take a short luxury taxi ride for an elevated modern Korean tasting menu experience.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light refreshment at the boutique hotel upon check-in or nearby traditional teahouse such as Cha Masineun Tteul
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul — modern Korean haute cuisine, tasting menu with wine pairing (reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light due to jet lag. Gyeongbokgung area is walkable and safe at night. December temperatures average -2°C to 5°C — pack a warm coat.

day_by_day.morning: Full immersive visit to Gyeongbokgung Palace including the Gyeonghoeru Pavilion and Hyangwonjeong Pond, stunning in winter. Witness the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (10:00 and 14:00). Consider renting a hanbok for complimentary palace entry and authentic photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Insadong, Seoul's premier cultural and antique district. Browse curated galleries, traditional craft shops, and the Ssamziegil courtyard complex. Visit Unhyeongung Palace — a lesser-known royal residence with intimate charm.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ikseon-dong Hanok Village, a trendy yet traditional alley district for cocktails at a stylish rooftop or basement bar. Dinner at Mingles (Michelin-starred, Gangnam) — creative Korean cuisine fusing global techniques.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or nearby Tosokchon Samgyetang for a warming ginseng chicken soup breakfast experience
meals.lunch: Jirisan — upscale traditional Korean set meal in Insadong area
meals.dinner: Mingles — signature Korean contemporary tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung Palace opens at 09:00. Hanbok rental shops are clustered near the palace east gate. Book Mingles well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon). The winter landscape with bare trees and frozen ponds is hauntingly beautiful. Guided tours of the Secret Garden run at set times — book the English tour in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Changgyeonggung Palace next door, then walk to the nearby National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) Seoul branch in the Gyeongbokgung compound for world-class Korean and international contemporary art.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at La Yeon (three Michelin stars, The Shilla Hotel) — the pinnacle of Korean fine dining with panoramic city views. After dinner, take a night drive to Namsan Tower for glittering winter city views.

meals.breakfast: Boutique hotel breakfast or Café Bora (iconic purple latte and traditional desserts, Bukchon branch)
meals.lunch: Balwoo Gongyang — temple food restaurant in Insadong, a rare and refined Buddhist vegetarian dining experience
meals.dinner: La Yeon at The Shilla Hotel — three Michelin stars, premium Korean kaiseki-style dinner

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours must be reserved ahead; English tours are limited. La Yeon requires formal attire and advance reservation. Namsan Tower cable car runs until 23:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day K-culture deep dive: arrange a bespoke Korean traditional arts workshop — choose from hanji (Korean paper craft), celadon pottery, or dancheong (traditional decorative painting) at the Korea Craft & Design Foundation in Insadong.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with lanterns in winter. Walk the Cheonggyecheon Stream promenade — a serene urban waterway lined with seasonal light installations.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Gwangjang Market for a premium street food tour — bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, and yukhoe (Korean beef tartare). Pair with makgeolli (Korean rice wine) at a traditional pojangmacha stall.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan bakery nearby such as Tartine Seoul (Bukchon branch)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a traditional tea house — Insadong Dawon for sujeonggwa (cinnamon punch) and tteok (rice cakes)
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market premium street food experience — curated tasting with a local food guide

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is best experienced in the evening when it's lively. A private food guide enhances the experience significantly. Cheonggyecheon winter light festival runs December–January.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the outskirts: Visit the UNESCO-listed Joseon Royal Tombs (Seooreung or Donggureung cluster) for a meditative winter morning walk through pine forests and ancient royal burial mounds — rarely crowded and deeply atmospheric.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Seoul. Afternoon at leisure in Samcheong-dong — a charming neighborhood of independent galleries, boutique design shops, and artisan cafés. Visit Gallery Hyundai or Kukje Gallery for premier Korean contemporary art.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Gaon (three Michelin stars, Gangnam) — the ultimate expression of refined Korean cuisine in an elegant setting with impeccable service. Post-dinner drinks at a rooftop bar in Gangnam.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Samcheong-dong café lunch — try Café de Leon or a seasonal Korean brunch spot
meals.dinner: Gaon — three Michelin stars, multi-course Korean fine dining

day_by_day.notes: Royal Tombs require a 30–40 min drive; arrange private car. Gaon is one of Seoul's hardest reservations — book months in advance. Dress code applies.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive K-beauty and wellness morning: Book a premium jjimjilbang (Korean spa) experience at Spa Lei or Dragon Hill Spa — enjoy the gender-separated hot spring pools, sauna rooms, and body scrub (Italy towel exfoliation) treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark — for design exhibitions and the Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. Browse the adjacent high-end fashion district.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Myeongdong for an evening stroll and street food sampling. Dinner at Hanilkwan — one of Seoul's oldest and most prestigious traditional Korean restaurants, famous for galbi-jjim (braised short ribs) and royal court cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel before spa
meals.lunch: Post-spa meal at a nearby Korean BBQ premium spot — Maple Tree House (Itaewon) for premium wagyu and Korean beef
meals.dinner: Hanilkwan — historic royal court Korean cuisine in an elegant traditional setting

day_by_day.notes: Book spa treatments in advance on weekends. DDP exhibitions change seasonally — check current schedule. Myeongdong is very busy on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private K-pop culture experience: Arrange a behind-the-scenes tour of HYBE Insight Museum (BTS, SEVENTEEN, etc.) in Yongsan — a premium interactive K-pop museum. Book VIP access for early entry and guided experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest and finest museums, housing 220,000+ artifacts including the iconic Gilt-bronze Maitreya Bodhisattva. Spend 2–3 hours exploring Korean history from prehistoric times to the Joseon Dynasty.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Dosa (Michelin-starred, Gangnam) for innovative Korean cuisine. Afterward, explore Itaewon's upscale cocktail bar scene — try Charles H at Four Seasons Hotel Seoul for award-winning craft cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Museum café at National Museum or nearby Yongsan premium dining
meals.dinner: Dosa — creative modern Korean tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: HYBE Insight requires advance booking; VIP slots sell out quickly. National Museum is free entry and closed Mondays — adjust if needed (check holiday schedule for December 2027).

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) — arrange a premium private guided tour to the Joint Security Area (JSA) at Panmunjom, the Third Infiltration Tunnel, and Dora Observatory for a sobering and historically profound experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue DMZ tour — visit Dorasan Station (the southernmost station of the Gyeongui Line) and the Peace Park. Return to Seoul by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening after an intense day. Dinner at Soigné (Michelin-starred) — intimate, creative contemporary cuisine. Early return to hotel for rest.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before DMZ departure (tours typically depart 07:30–08:00)
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch box or DMZ area restaurant included in private tour
meals.dinner: Soigné — intimate Michelin-starred contemporary dining

day_by_day.notes: JSA tours require passport and advance registration (minimum 48–72 hours). US and some other citizens have specific restrictions. Use a reputable licensed tour operator. Dress code: no ripped jeans, camouflage, or shorts at JSA.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park for a winter morning hike — choose the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail for stunning views of the ancient fortress walls draped in snow or frost. Moderate 3–4 hour hike with spectacular Seoul skyline panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return and refresh. Afternoon visit to the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Asia's premier private art museums featuring traditional Korean art alongside world-class contemporary works by Damien Hirst, Jeff Koons, and Korean masters.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Mosu Seoul (Michelin two stars) — chef Sung Anh's globally inspired Korean cuisine. Post-dinner: Gangnam rooftop bar experience at CLOUD 36 or Sky Lounge for festive December city lights.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at hotel before hike
meals.lunch: Post-hike restorative meal — Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) at a traditional restaurant near Bukhansan
meals.dinner: Mosu Seoul — two Michelin stars, seasonal Korean tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Wear proper hiking boots and thermal layers for Bukhansan in December. Trails can be icy — microspike crampons recommended (available for rent near trailhead). Leeum closed Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private Korean cooking class at a premium culinary studio — learn to prepare royal court cuisine dishes such as gujeolpan (nine-sectioned platter), japchae, and kimchi from a master chef. Take home a handwritten recipe booklet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon in the upscale Cheongdam-dong and Apgujeong Rodeo Street area — Seoul's answer to Paris's Avenue Montaigne. Browse flagship stores of Korean luxury brands (MCM, Gentle Monster, Tamburins) and international maisons.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas Eve dinner at Yonsei Severance — or opt for a premium hotel Christmas Eve gala dinner at The Shilla Seoul or Four Seasons Hotel Seoul, featuring live music, festive decorations, and a multi-course celebratory menu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Upscale lunch in Apgujeong — Dosan Park area restaurants such as Evett or Onjium
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve Gala Dinner at Four Seasons Hotel Seoul — festive multi-course dinner with wine pairing and live entertainment

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is extremely festive in Seoul — the city lights up beautifully. Book Christmas Eve dinner months in advance. Cheongdam-dong area has spectacular holiday decorations.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning at leisure — sleep in and enjoy a luxurious hotel breakfast. Optional: attend a Christmas service at Myeongdong Cathedral, one of Korea's most beautiful Catholic churches, for a cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory (123rd floor) — the world's fifth-tallest building with breathtaking 360° views of Seoul on a clear winter day. Explore Lotte World Mall for premium shopping and festive atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas dinner at Kwon Sooksoo — intimate, reservation-only Korean fine dining by celebrated chef Kwon Woo-joong, known for extraordinary seasonal Korean cuisine. One of Seoul's most exclusive dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel Christmas breakfast
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Lotte World Tower — Sky31 Club or The Palace restaurant
meals.dinner: Kwon Sooksoo — exclusive private Korean fine dining (advance reservation essential, very limited seats)

day_by_day.notes: Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory: book timed-entry tickets online. Kwon Sooksoo is one of Seoul's most difficult reservations — contact well in advance. Many restaurants close Christmas Day; confirm reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Final cultural immersion: Visit the National Palace Museum of Korea (within Gyeongbokgung complex) for an in-depth look at Joseon Dynasty royal artifacts, then walk to the Seoul Museum of History nearby for a comprehensive overview of the city's transformation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell shopping in Bukchon and Insadong — pick up premium Korean souvenirs: handcrafted celadon ceramics, hanji paper goods, premium gochujang and doenjang sets, Korean teas, and K-beauty luxury products from Sulwhasoo or History of Whoo flagship stores.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Onjium (Michelin-starred) — the most authentic expression of Joseon royal court cuisine in a stunning traditional hanok setting, a perfect culinary bookend to the trip. Post-dinner: rooftop drinks with a view at Bukchon or Anguk area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — linger and enjoy
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang — the legendary ginseng chicken restaurant near Gyeongbokgung for a nostalgic farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Onjium — Michelin-starred Joseon royal court cuisine in a traditional hanok

day_by_day.notes: Onjium requires advance reservation and is one of Seoul's most culturally significant dining experiences. Allow extra time for final shopping — Sulwhasoo flagship in Insadong is unmissable for luxury K-beauty.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning. Enjoy a last hotel breakfast. Take a quiet farewell walk through Bukchon Hanok Village in the crisp morning air — peaceful before the crowds arrive. Visit a nearby café for a final Korean coffee or traditional tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from boutique stay. Private luxury chauffeur transfer to Incheon International Airport (allow 90 minutes for the journey plus buffer time). Enjoy the premium airport facilities — Incheon's Terminal 1 and 2 offer excellent lounges, duty-free shopping, and Korean cultural exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Carry fond memories of 13 extraordinary days in Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor it
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a nearby café or hotel — try patbingsu (red bean shaved ice) as a sweet goodbye even in winter, or doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean stew) for warmth
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Incheon — Korean Air First Class Lounge or premium airport restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00–12:00; request late checkout if flight allows. Incheon Airport has a Korean Cultural Street with traditional performances and exhibits — arrive early to enjoy. Duty-free at Incheon is world-class for final K-beauty and Korean spirit (soju, makgeolli) purchases.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX
